_comment: Average cold rent (Kaltmiete) per m2/month, used to estimate gross rental yield for the minRoiPercent job filter. Re-derived in July 2026 from sourced price-per-sqm x reported gross-yield/Mietspiegel data across two research passes (see the 'Where to point Fredy' research artifact). A third pass (also July 2026) added district/area-level breakdowns for the active Invest-job cities, sourced from official Mietspiegel documents where available (Aalen, Villingen-Schwenningen: real Wohnlage-zone data extracted directly from the source PDF; Offenburg, Fulda: official citywide average only, no area breakdown exists in their Mietspiegel methodology) and from a market-rate aggregator (mietspiegeltabelle.de, 'VALUE Marktdatenbank') for Dresden/Leipzig/Moenchengladbach, since their official Mietspiegel PDFs could not be extracted (scanned/binary PDFs) - those three cities' area figures reflect current asking rent, not the legally-defined (lower) Mietspiegel average, which is arguably more relevant for a new landlord's achievable rent anyway. Schwaebisch Hall/Walldorf/Wiesloch have no official Mietspiegel at all; their figures are unofficial portal averages, flagged accordingly. A fourth pass (August 2026) added the towns actually turning up in the '1.Invest 200k - Nordschwarzwald' and '2.Invest 200k- (Umkreis Vaihingen/Enz)' jobs (picked by frequency in real listing results, not by geography alone), sourced from live market-data aggregators (miet-check.de, mietspiegeltabelle.de, ohne-makler.net, immoportal.com, immoreport.de, miete-aktuell.de - current asking-rent figures, same 'Sollmiete over blended Mietspiegel' reasoning as the third pass) since wohnungsboerse.net (used in earlier passes) has gone dead and now redirects to ImmoScout24's homepage. Ludwigsburg is a known outlier worth flagging: its official city Mietspiegel gives ~10.66/m2 (existing-tenant blended average) vs 14.73/m2 here (current asking rent) - the gap is unusually wide for this pass, kept as asking rent for consistency with the rest of the file's Sollmiete framing, but worth a gut-check against a real listing before trusting it heavily. Schoemberg here is the Landkreis Calw one (near Bad Wildbad), not the unrelated Zollernalbkreis Schoemberg - a real substring-matching ambiguity if a future job ever surfaces listings from the other one. Re-check periodically (immoscout24 Mietspiegel, empirica, local Gutachterausschuss) and edit this file freely - Fredy reloads it automatically on change. A fifth pass (August 2026) re-anchored the Ludwigsburg/Vaihingen-Enz job cluster (ludwigsburg, asperg, bietigheim-bissingen, ditzingen, freiberg am neckar, vaihingen an der enz, leonberg) away from asking-rent portal averages to official Mietspiegel figures, after the asking-rent numbers turned out to run meaningfully hot versus the qualified indices: Ludwigsburg's own qualified Mietspiegel 2025 gives 10.66/m2 (vs. 14.73 here previously); asperg/bietigheim-bissingen/ditzingen/freiberg-am-neckar/vaihingen-an-der-enz are derived from Ludwigsburg's 10.66 via the percentage price offsets in the region's own 'Dokumentation einfache Mietspiegel im Raum Ludwigsburg 2024' (Ulrich Stein, commissioned by DMB-Mieterbund Ludwigsburg and Haus & Grund Region Ludwigsburg); leonberg is read directly off its own qualified Mietspiegel 2023/2024 Basismiete table, a blended figure for a ~60-65sqm flat with standard/neutral fittings across all Baujahr bands (no single headline average exists in that document - it's a full size x age matrix). sachsenheim, eppingen and lauffen am neckar are still asking-rent-portal figures, unchanged and un-re-verified this pass: eppingen has an official qualified Mietspiegel (Landkreis Heilbronn-Suedwest, 26-municipality collaborative index) but no single figure could be pulled quickly; sachsenheim and lauffen am neckar have no qualified/official index at all, confirmed for lauffen am neckar, inferred for sachsenheim from its absence in the Ludwigsburg-region document above. A quick follow-up correction the same day: leonberg raised to 11 (user judgment call, between the 9.1 blended-Mietspiegel-table estimate and the original 14.45 portal figure) and vaihingen an der enz raised to 10.2 (split between the 8.71 official-anchor derivation above and the ~11.26 EUR/m2 Q1 2026 portal average, since the -18.3% Ludwigsburg offset was calibrated in 2024 against an older Ludwigsburg Mietspiegel edition and may have drifted from current reality).
